title: To make technical amendments to certain marine fish conservation statutes, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(Sec.1)This bill amends the Billfish Conservation Act of 2012 to limit the sale of billfish caught by U.S. fishing vessels.

Under current law, billfish that are caught by U.S. vessels and landed (unloaded onshore) in Hawaii or Pacific Insular Areas (American Samoa, Baker Island, Guam, Howland Island, Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, Kingman Reef, Midway Island, the Northern Mariana Islands, Palmyra Atoll, and Wake Island) may be sold and exported to non-U.S. markets or transported to other U.S. markets.

This bill requires billfish caught by U.S. vessels and landed in Hawaii or Pacific Insular Areas to be retained for sale in those areas.

summary.headline: This law changes rules on selling billfish caught by U.S. boats and landed in Hawaii or U.S. Pacific island areas.
summary.what_it_does: It amends the Billfish Conservation Act of 2012, which covers fish such as marlin and swordfish. Before this change, billfish caught by U.S. vessels and unloaded in Hawaii or the Pacific Insular Areas could be sold abroad or shipped to other U.S. markets. Under this law, those billfish must be kept for sale within Hawaii or the Pacific Insular Areas.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial fishing vessel operators who catch billfish and land them in Hawaii or Pacific Insular Areas
who_it_affects.how: They must keep billfish landed in those areas for sale there rather than selling them abroad or shipping them to other U.S. markets.

who_it_affects.group: Seafood buyers and dealers in Hawaii and the Pacific Insular Areas
who_it_affects.how: They can count on billfish landed locally being available for sale in those areas.

who_it_affects.group: Seafood buyers and dealers in other U.S. states and foreign countries
who_it_affects.how: They can no longer buy billfish caught by U.S. vessels and landed in Hawaii or the Pacific Insular Areas for resale outside those areas.
